content: Both lamivudine and zidovudine are associated with an increased risk of developing immune reconstitution syndrome. Similarly, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (DF) and zidovudine also elevate the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Lamivudine has a minor pharmacodynamic synergistic effect that enhances the activity of zidovudine. The clinical significance of this interaction is either minor or currently unknown, but it is considered a beneficial synergism. In the United States, approximately 7% of the reference population is affected. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advises against breastfeeding for HIV-infected women due to the potential risk of postnatal HIV transmission to their infants. The use of antiretroviral therapy (ART) during pregnancy is generally considered acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated any evidence of fetal risk. Doravirine is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) that inhibits HIV-1 replication by noncompetitive inhibition of the HIV-1 reverse transcriptase enzyme. Lamivudine, a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI), requires phosphorylation to its active metabolite, which then inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase by causing DNA chain termination after incorporation into the viral DNA. Tenofovir DF, also an NRTI, undergoes hydrolysis and subsequent phosphorylation to inhibit HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with the natural substrate deoxyadenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP). It also causes DNA chain termination after incorporation into the viral DNA. Doravirine is primarily metabolized by the CYP3A enzyme. Lamivudine undergoes minor metabolism via CYP3A, while tenofovir alafenamide (AF) does not involve CYP metabolism. A complete antiretroviral regimen for adults with HIV who have no prior ART treatment history should not be co-prescribed with other antiretroviral therapies. Patients should be instructed to take their medication at a consistent time each day. The medication can be taken with or without food. The medication should be stored at a temperature of 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions to 15–30°C (59–86°F). It must be kept in its original bottle, tightly closed to protect it from moisture, and desiccants should not be removed.
